status_summary: Executive Order 14184 (2025-01-27) directed reinstatement at former rank with back pay and benefits, and DOD announced an outreach program on 2025-04-23 for roughly 8,700 separated members (a July 2026 report puts involuntary separations at nearly 8,000). Uptake has been small: 13 had returned by late June 2025, and in July 2026 the Pentagon put returns at about 230, while a 2026-07-23 report gave about 200 troops and 85 Coast Guard members reinstated, nearly 900 discharge upgrades, and more than 800 who had expressed interest. The window to rejoin was extended on 2026-03-23 to 2027-04-01 and the service obligation for returnees was cut from four years to two. Under DOD policy back pay is reduced by interim civilian income and VA payments, and some applicants described waits of months to over a year.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14184 signed. It directs DOD and DHS to offer reinstatement at former rank with full back pay, benefits, and bonuses to members discharged solely for refusing the vaccine, and to report progress within 60 days.
Secretary Hegseth announces the reinstatement outreach program at the Army War College; roughly 8,700 members are eligible and the offer is to stay open one year.
Reporting finds only 13 former members had returned to service after the outreach and back-pay offer.
Hegseth extends the invitation to return to 2027-04-01 and cuts the active-service commitment for returnees from four years to two.

A Secretary of War memo (header date appears to be about 2026-05-07, URL dated 2026-05-08) continues the program for another year and directs correction boards to treat discharges tied only to vaccine refusal as presumptively unjust, with discharge upgrades and record corrections available even to those who do not return. The text reviewed does not address back pay or rank.

A Pentagon official says about 230 former members have rejoined (about 2.7 percent of those eligible) and that more than 600 have expressed interest. DOD announces a panel to study the mandate decision and to declassify related materials.
Military Times reports roughly 200 troops and 85 Coast Guard members reinstated, nearly 900 discharge upgrades, back pay reduced by offsets, and delays for some applicants.

title: Reinstate members discharged over the COVID-19 vaccine, with rank and back pay
uncertainties: Counts differ between Military Times reports (about 230 rejoined on 2026-07-16 versus about 200 troops plus 85 Coast Guard members a week later); they were not reconciled. No primary document confirms how rank restoration works in practice or whether any back pay has been paid in full; the May 2026 memo text reviewed was an OCR copy and did not address pay. The 2025-06-30 return count comes from a search-result headline and snippet that was not opened. The Military.com and Military Times pieces are news reports; no court challenge to this program was found. Update 2026-10-15: one search for post-July figures returned only earlier reports.
